headline: Recommended a contract with Maintenance Tech. Inc. to replace vehicle wash systems at the Quick Turnaround Facility.
summary: Briefings covered the City's artificial intelligence policy, jet fuel taxes, and long waits for evening arrivals. Staff also gave updates on construction, finances, and airport operations.

Approved the minutes as presented, including the October 7, 2026 meeting, 5-0.

plain_text:
PATRICK LEAHY BURLINGTON INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT  
BOARD OF AIRPORT COMMISSIONERS 
 MINUTES OF MEETING  
November 4, 2026 
Location: Large Conference Room (Room 337) 
 Patrick Leahy Burlington International Airport, Third Floor 
1200 Airport Drive, 
South Burlington, VT 05403 
[Hybrid meeting]          
MEMBERS PRESENT:  Tim George, Chair  
Jeff Schulman, Vice Chair  
    Helen Riehle  
Al Turkos 
Chip Mason 
Andrew Savage   
MEMBERS ABSENT:  Robin Guillian  
BTV STAFF PRESENT:  Nicolas Longo, Director of Aviation  
Larry Lackey, Director of Planning, Engineering and Sustainability 
David Carman, Deputy Director – Airport Operations 
Marie Friedman, Director of Finance 
Romeo von Hermann, Customer Experience Manager 
Jesse Sprague, Executive Assistant 
Andrew Geppner, Airfield Manager 
OTHERS PRESENT:   CCTV 
 
1.0 Call to Order  
1.1 Call to Order 
Commission Chair Tim George called the meeting to order at 4:01 P.M. 
1.2 Acknowledgement of Remote Commissioners 
Commissioners attending the meeting remotely identified themselves (Chip Mason) 
 
2.0 Agenda 
2.1 Approve/Adopt Agenda  
MOTION by Al Turkos, SECOND by Helen Riehle to approve the agenda as presented.  
VOTING: unanimous (5-0), motion carried.
3.0 Public Forum 
3.1 The following members of the public made public comment, in the below order, regarding 
the respective topics: 
3.1.1  No members of the public chose to speak at public forum 
 
4.0 Consent agenda: 
4.1 Approval of the minutes 
MOTION by Commissioner Helen Riehle, SECOND by Commissioner Al Turkos, to 
approve the minutes as presented in the agenda packet, including Minutes from the October 
7, 2026 meeting.   
VOTING: unanimous (5-0); motion carried. 
 
 
 
5.0 Presentation on City of Burlington Artificial Intelligence Policy 
5.1 Presentation on City of Burlington Artificial Intelligence Policy, N. Longo, S. Barker 
Commissioner Jeff Schulman joined the meeting in person at 4:05 
5.1.1 City of Burlington’s Chief Innovation Officer, Scot Barker, provided an 
overview of the City’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) policy. The City allows 
employees to use Microsoft Copilot in specific contexts and for specific 
purposes. The policy is written to protect data sovereignty within the City.  
5.1.2 Director Longo said that the Airport is looking into AI camera system to track 
airline performance standards.  
5.1.3 Scot Barker said that the AI policy is for every City of Burlington department. 
The policy tells employees when to use AI and how to cite it.  
 
6.0 Action Items 
6.1 Request to Sign Contract with Maintenance Tech. Inc. 
MOTION by Commissioner Helen Riehle, SECOND by Commissioner Al Turkos, to 
recommend the Board of Finance and City Council approve the contract with Maintenance 
Tech. Inc to replace the automated vehicle wash systems in the Quick Turnaround Facility 
(QTA). 
DISCUSSION was led by Director Longo, and included the following details, in addition to 
the memo: 
- The Quick Turnaround (QTA) facility is an onsite site facility used by car rental 
companies to detail, wash and fuel rental cars.  
- Customer Facility Charges (CFCs) are funding this project and are collected through 
every rental car reservation at Leahy BTV. These funds must be approved by the rental 
car companies for projects that support rental car operations at the Airport.  
- Per the City of Burlington procurement policy, this request can be approved by the Board 
of Finance and does not need to be approved by City Council, as this request is below 
$500,000.  
- CFCs are primarily generated from passengers whose destination is BTV and choose to 
rent a car at the airport.
- The new steel system will preserve the overall system and allow larger sized vehicles to 
use the services provided by the QTA, and the new equipment should last longer than the 
previous equipment.  
VOTING: unanimous (6-0); motion carried.  
  
 
7.0 Quarterly Airport Operations Update  
7.1 Quarterly Airport Operations Update, D. Carman 
7.2 Presentation by Deputy Director of Airport Operations Dave Carman. 
DISCUSSION and presentation included: 
7.2.1 Review of the Full Scale Exercise (FSE), which took place on September 12. 
The FSE was a formal test of emergency responses at the Airport, as required 
by the FAA every three years. The exercise incorporated participation by the 
National Disaster Medical System (NDMS).  
7.2.2 5K Run on the runway took place on October 3, with 500 runners 
participating in the race. 
7.2.3 Deputy Director Carman and Airport Operations Manager Stacy Leveille 
attended the Runway Safety Summit in Worcester Massachusetts.  
7.2.4 Leahy BTV has submitted its final Safety Management Systems (SMS) 
manual to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) for final review 
7.2.5 Construction on the Cargo Apron has begun to expand the apron for cargo 
operations, as well as the Snow Removal Equipment building, which will 
house snow removal equipment once the project is complete.  
7.2.6 Airfield Manager Andrew Geppner talked about preparedness and equipment 
used for the upcoming snow season, including the FAA approved sand that is 
put on the runway during snow events and the brooms for snow equipment. 
 
 
8.0 Construction Update 
8.1 Construction Update, L. Lackey 
8.1.1 In addition to the written update provided to the Airport Commission, Director of 
Engineering and Sustainability Larry Lackey highlighted the following updates 
and projects: 
1. Glycol recycling project and centralized de-icing project  
2. Cargo apron project 
3. Residential sound insulation program construction work on homes near 
the airport 
 
9.0 Residential Sound Insulation Program Updates 
9.1 Residential Sound Insulation Program Updates, L. Lackey 
9.1.1 In addition to the written update provided to the Airport Commission, Director of 
Engineering and Sustainability Larry Lackey highlighted the following updates: 
1. The RSIP report is current; Phase 7 is proceeding with the RSIP. 
2. The RSIP continues for homeowners that may be interested in the 
program in the future. 
 
10.0  Financial Update  
10.1 Financial Update 
10.1.1 In addition to the written update provided to the Airport Commission, Director of 
Finance Marie Friedman highlighted the following updates: 
1. Revenues are coming in ahead of last year.
2. Expenses were planned to increase and are increasing. 
3. Grant projection season will slow down.  
 
11.0 Director’s Report 
11.1 Director’s Report, N. Longo 
11.1.1 In addition to the written presentation, Director Longo reported: 
1. Second floor renovation is underway; in a few weeks, the entire 
renovation will be open. Half of the renovation is open currently.  
2. Report on electric vehicle charging at the Airport, including: electric 
rental cars, chargers on the airfield and parking garage, opportunities to 
add more electric vehicle charging and more electric vehicles within the 
airport fleet.  
3. Current leases and contract negotiations include: 
• Heritage Aviation Lease 
• Hudson News Contract Amendment 
• Airline Use License Agreement  
• Rental Car Contract 
• Beta Technologies Lease Amendment 
4. Upcoming in 2027: Request for Proposals for food concessions at the 
Airport  
5. Data for parking garage statistics represent the averages based on staff 
sampling in the garage.  
6. Leahy BTV has 19 nonstop destinations; a net total of 7 destinations 
have been added compared to 12 destinations in 2017. 
 
12.0 Commissioner Items 
12.1 Discussion on community feedback regarding nighttime arrivals at BTV, C. Mason 
12.1.1 Commissioner Chip Mason stated that he received a communication from a 
community member asking about long wait times on evening arrivals between 
the time a plan lands and when the passenger exits the parking garage.  
12.1.2 Director Longo detailed that wait times can happen when multiple planes arrive 
not as scheduled but early. Ground crews take the planes one at a time, and 
planes who are early must wait to deplane, so the aircraft ends up sitting longer 
before deplaning. It has been reported to Leahy BTV that flight crews are not 
always accurately reporting the correct reason for wait times.  
12.1.3 The Airport has a helpdesk form on the website on the Lost and Found page 
where passengers can submit feedback.  
 
13.0 Follow Up Items 
13.1 Jet Fuel Taxes 
13.1.1 Director Nicolas Longo reviewed that all taxes collected on jet fuel sales must be 
returned to an aviation program. Director Longo continued conversations with 
the City of South Burlington on the collection of these taxes. The 1% local option 
tax on jet fuel must be used for aeronautical purposes. There is also a 6% state 
sales tax. Leahy BTV continues to request these funds return to Leahy BTV. In 
South Burlington, there is no city aviation program for these funds to be used.  
13.2 Artificial Intelligence
13.2.1 This item will be removed in future meetings as it was addressed in the 
Director’s Report.  
 
14.0 Adjournment 
MOTION by Commissioner Andrew Savage, SECOND by Commissioner Helen Riehle, to 
adjourn the meeting.  
VOTING: unanimous (6-0); motion carried.  Meeting Adjourned at 6:11 P.M.
